title: This Tiny Bat Was Clocked at 99 Miles an Hour

scenes.text: This tiny bat was clocked at ninety-nine miles an hour.
It's the Mexican free-tailed bat, small enough to fit in your hand.
In 2016, researchers tracked one from aircraft and measured about ninety-nine miles an hour.
That's one of the fastest level flights ever measured.
In Texas, nearly twenty million of them live in one cave.
They pour out at dusk like smoke. Tiny bats, ninety-nine miles an hour.

description:
A Mexican free-tailed bat was tracked at about 99 mph ground speed in a 2016 study.
At Bracken Cave in Texas, nearly 20 million of them roost together.
Would you watch the sunset flight?
first_comment: The researchers noted wind could have helped, so the true airspeed is uncertain. Still wild. Fastest animal you know?
